messages:
maria: quick post-release quickcheck after the 08:00 rollout — running the standard routing+health probes now
deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-20.v12 -> v13 completed, canary 10% -> ramping rules applied :rocket:
ian: saw a ~3m window of 502/504s from the embeddings endpoint (us-west1) right after the rollout
matt: confirming, traces show repeated proxy upstream resets. model pods seem healthy and not OOMing, but proxy CPU climbs to ~80%
sasha-oncall: EU region also shows a tiny bump in 5xxs, but latency OK. spike correlates with a batch of long-seq requests at T+2m
jules: curious — routing policy for v13 includes fallback: cost-optimized (route->v13 -> v12 if latent). Could the fallback create oscillation under high concurrency?
maria: can someone paste the short trace from the synthetic probe?
sasha-oncall: paste below:
```
> curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"long text..."}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: envoy
Upstream-Status: reset
Body: {"error":"upstream connection reset"}
```
matt: logs from envoy show repeated connect failures to v13 instances then immediate fallback to v12; fallback traffic is large and seems to saturate the proxy process, triggering more connect churn
ian: hypothesis: fallback thrash -> proxy CPU -> more timeouts -> more fallback. cascading loop. not a model-serving crash, more control-plane/routing feedback loop
ops-bot: alert triggered: proxy_cpu > 75% (us-west1) for 4m — paging to oncall
maria: options: 1) rollback v13 entirely 2) pin routing in affected regions to v12 3) disable variant fallback temporarily. prefer minimal blast radius (2 or 3)
jules: disabling fallback at the routing layer is fastest. command: `redwoodctl routing update --policy default --no-fallback --regions us-west1,eu1`
matt: i can push that now and watch probes. will also bump proxy replicate count as short-term relief
sasha-oncall: while you do that, i'll create a dedicated quickcheck for long-sequence embedding flows (every 30s) in those regions
maria: do it. decision: disable fallback in us-west1+eu1, pin apac to v12 for 45m, monitor 30m, then re-evaluate. no full rollback unless errors persist after mitigations
ian: add an alert rule: if 5xx rate > 0.5% AND proxy_cpu > 70% for 5m -> page and post in #incidents
matt: applied routing change — `routing.default.fallback = false` in control plane. proxy replica +1 applied to us-west1 pool. watching metrics: 5xx down to baseline in 90s
sasha-oncall: quickcheck results: embedding probe 30s x6 -> all green, no upstream reset traces
maria: good. i'll update release notes with a short "mitigation: routing fallback disabled in us-west1/eu1; pinned apac to v12 temporarily" and flag for postmortem if it reoccurs
jules: follow-up todo: investigate why fallback load is so heavy (request fanout or naive client retries). suggest adding smoothing/backoff in routing logic
ian: opened ticket INF-4283 with initial notes and traces
maria: thanks team. leave the pin for 45m, i'll post back here at +40m to decide re-enable or rollback
deploy-bot: action record: routing.fallback disabled (us-west1,eu1), apac pinned to v12 until +2700s by maria
matt: great work. closing the quickcheck thread but keeping monitoring up :thumbsup:
